Organic sulfonates, phosphonates, and thiophosphonates are classes of organophosphorus compounds that have been widely used as insecticides in agriculture and pest control. These compounds act by inhibiting the enzyme acetylcholinesterase in insects, which disrupts their nervous system function.

Some well-known examples include:
- Malathion (an organophosphate insecticide)
- Parathion (an organophosphate insecticide)
- Chlorpyrifos (an organophosphate insecticide)

While these compounds have other applications (some sulfonates are used as detergents, and some phosphonates are used as chelating agents), their most common and significant collective use is as insecticides.
